chunks.text: Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 IN THE COURT OF Ms. CHHAVI KAPOOR SPECIAL JUDGE (PC ACT) (CBI)-07 ROUSE AVENUE COURTS NEW DELHI CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CC No. 374/2019 RC No. 2172016A0011/ACU-V/AC-II/CBI/New Delhi dated U/Sec.: 120B, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and 13 (1) (d) read with Sec. 13 (2) of The Prevention of Corruption Act Central Bureau of Vs. 1. Swarn Singh Malhi, Investigation S/o Late Sardar Jamar Singh, R/o 2925, Ground Floor, Dharampura, Gandhi Nagar, Delhi. (Permanent Address :- Hansawala, Tehsil Tarantaran, District Amritsar, Punjab). Saroj Bala, W/o Sh. Brij Mohan, R/o 2195/7A, Housing Board Colony, Faridabad, Haryana. CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 1 of 210 Neeru Kumar Gupta, S/o Late Sh. Panna Lal Gupta, R/o G-2/78, Sector-16, Rohini, Delhi-110089. Sangeeta Gupta, W/o Sh. Neeru Kumar Gupta, R/o G-2/78, Sector-16, Rohini, Delhi-110089. Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 Date of institution : 31.03.2017 Judgment Reserved on : 01.12.2025 Date of Judgment : 08.12.2025 JUDGMENT FACTS

This case was registered on the basis of source information against one Sh. H. R. Sapra, the then Dy. Secretary (Alternative) (retired), Land & Building Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, New Delhi, Sh. Swarn Singh Malhi (S.S. Malhi- Accused No.1), the then UDC/Dealing Clerk (retired), Land & Building Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, New Delhi, Sh. Neeru Kumar Gupta @N.K. Gupta, Advocate, (private person-A-3). Smt. Suman D/o Sh. Dharm Dev, other unknown public servants and other unknown private persons Under Section 120-B r/w Section 419, CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 2 of 210 420, 467, 468 & 471 IPC and Section 13(2) r/w 13 (1) (d) of P.C. Act, 1988. It is the claim of CBI that it was during the investigation of one of the Land & Building department fraudulent recommendation cases i.e. RC 4 /2015/CBI/AC-II/ACU-7 VI/New Delhi that the original file of Land &Building Department regarding allotment of plot in the name of one Smt. Suman was recovered from the residence of accused Sh. N. K. Gupta (Accused No.3) during search. Consequent to verification, this recommendation was revealed as a fraudulent one and hence, the present case was registered.

It is the case of CBI that Government of NCT of Delhi had launched a welfare scheme to rehabilitate and compensate the agriculturist whose lands were acquired by the Government and The Land & Building Department was implementing the said scheme for allotment of alternative plots in lieu of acquired land under the scheme of "Large Scale Acquisition Development & Disposal of Land in Delhi" announced by Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs vide letter No. 37/16/60- Delhi dated 2nd May, 1961 . In order to implement this scheme, the Land & Building Department used to invite applications from the land owners whose lands were acquired by the Government for grant of alternative plots through press advertisements. In case the applicant was the recorded owner at the time of notification u/s 4 of Land Acquisition Act, the following documents were required to be submitted along with the application: A) Revenue record , Jamabandi , Khatoni Mutation which ever is applicable. CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 3 of 210 B) Payment certificate issued by LAC/SDM. Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 C)Affidavit that the applicant / dependent does not own any property in any urban area , New Delhi , Cantt. Area. D)Two passport sized photographs, three specimen signature , copy of election ID Card / ration card , duly attested by gazette officer. E) order of ADJ for compensation / probate / sale / mutation if applicable. F) Indemnity bond registered with the Sub Registrar Delhi

It is the case of CBI that as per the procedure prescribed in the above said Guidelines, on receipt of application from the applicant i.e. the owner whose land was acquired by the Government, the contents of the application forms were verified from the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) concerned. The Revenue Records filed by the applicant was also verified by the Revenue staff of Land & Building Dept. and the applicant was called for personal verification. Thereafter, the case of the applicant was put for final consideration by the committee constituted for the purpose for approval and for issue of recommendation to the DDA for allotment of alternative plot. The plots were allotted by DDA through draw of lots and such allotments were based on the recommendation letters issued by Land & Building Department in favor of allottee as per policy laid down in this regard by the Government of Delhi.

It is claimed in the FIR that the above named accused criminally conspired with each other and used forged documents to get CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 4 of 210 recommendation for allotment of a plot measuring 80 Sq yards in the name of one Smt. Suman D/o Dharm Dev, Chirag Delhi, based on which DDA issued allotment letter qua a plot no. 470, Sector-19, Dwarka, New Delhi measuring 67 Sq. meter to this person .It is claimed by CBI that Shri Swarn Singh Malhi , the then dealing assistant i.e. Accused No. 1 and Shri H R Sapra , the then Under Secretary processed the application of this person . i.e Smt. Suman and placed forged documents before the recommendation committee which later went on to approve the recommendation for allotment of an alternative plot to her. This plot was recommended in lieu of acquired land of Khasra no. 461/2 , Village Jaitpur vide award no. 2/90-91 dated 06.04.1990 for which compensation of Rs. 34.694.41 had been paid to the rightful owners. It is the case of CBI that investigation revealed that the said acquired land of Khasra No 461/2 , Village Jaitpur actually belonged to one Sh. Laabh Singh and Sh. Thakar Singh, both sons of Late Sh. Ghuma Singh who had claimed the compensation on 23.10.1991 from the government .It is alleged by CBI that a person namely Ms. Suman had impersonated as the owner of the acquired land in the application form submitted and she succeeded in getting the recommendation letter issued in her name from Land and Building Department. CBI claimed that their investigation revealed that this person Suman was a fictitious person as she was not found existing or residing at her last reported address. As per the chargesheet, vide notification u/s 4 of LA.

Act, 1984 dated 02.06.1909, lands of village Jaitpur were notified for acquisition by Delhi Administration and plot bearing Khasra No 461/2 was included CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 5 of 210 in the said notification. Thereafter, vide section 6 declaration dated 10.07.190- LAC was directed to take acquisition of lands notified u/s 4 of the said Act and plot bearing khasra no. 461/2 was the included in the list of lands. The investigation of CBI has revealed that award no 2/90-91 of acquired land of village Jaitpur was announced in the open court on 26.04.1990 wherein the details of land owner who had claimed for compensation for their acquired land was given .It is the case of CBI that plot no. 461/2 was in the name of Sh. Laabh Singh and Sh. Thakar Singh, both sons of Sh. Ghuma Singh and compensation of Rs. 69308.91 in lieu of acquisition of plot no. 461/2 was given solely to Sh. Thakar Singh on 23.10.1991 at the request of Sh. Laabh Singh.

It is the case of CBI that as per the procedure prescribed in the above said Guidelines, on receipt of application from the applicant i.e. the owner whose land was acquired by the Government, the contents of the application forms were verified from the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) concerned. The Revenue Records filed by the applicant was also verified by the Revenue staff of Land & Building Dept. and the applicant was called for personal verification. Thereafter, the case of the applicant was put for final consideration by the committee constituted for the purpose for approval and for issue of recommendation to the DDA for allotment of alternative plot. The plots were allotted by DDA through draw of lots and such allotments were based on the recommendation letters issued by Land & Building Department in favor of allottee as per policy laid down in this regard by the Government of Delhi.

CBI has claimed that their investigation has further revealed that the farmers whose lands were acquired by the award no. 2/90-91 could have also applied for the allotment of alternative plots as per the above mentioned policy of Government of India . Hence as per the laid down norm by Land & Building Department, each application was allotted a number according to the File Head Register. In the allotted number, 32 was denoting "South Zone" and 55 was denoting "village Jaitpur". A separate file for each application was created and submitted to the branch officer and while submitting the application, details of the application viz name, details of acquired land, village name, award number etc. was maintained after checking in the noting file by dealing assistant of the branch. Thereafter, the dealing assistant would seek LAC report in a prescribed format on the application. The CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 6 of 210 LAC report used to contain the date of notification u/s 4 of Land Acquisition Act (LA Act)-1982, name of the recorded owner of the land at the time of publication of said notification, khasra number with area, share of the applicant, amount of compensation with date of payment to the applicant, and date of taking of possession by the Government. After receipt of LAC report, the file was again submitted by the dealing assistant with a proposal to seek report from Tehsildar. L&B Dept. and Tehsildar used to submit his report with regard to notification of land u/s 22(1) of DDA Act . On receipt of report from Tehsildar, the file was sent to the writ cell for legal scrutiny by law officers. After obtaining legal opinion, a detailed brief of file was prepared by the dealing clerk and it was signed by the Branch Officer for placing the same before recommendation committee which consisted of Secretary cum Commissioner, Joint Secretary, Law Officer and Branch Head. Once the meeting of recommendation committee was held, the minutes of the same were drawn which contained the details of decision taken in the said meeting. Thereafter, recommendation letter signed by Joint Secretary (Land &Building Department) was sent to DDA for allotment of alternative plot.

The investigation of CBI has revealed that a meeting of the recommendation committee consisting of Sh. R. Chandra Mohan, Secretary cum Commissioner, Smt.Asha Nayyar, Addl. Secretary, Sh. Diwakar Singh, ALA and Sh. H. R. Sapra, Dy Secretary (Alt) was held on 15.01.1999 and in the said meeting 27 cases were placed before the committee for consideration. For each case, separate summary sheets CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 7 of 210 had been prepared and signed after detailed examination by the Dy. Secretary (Alt) and ALA. Based on the summary sheets and discussions, 15 Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 cases were recommended by the committee whereas two (02) cases were recommended for re-examination and ten (10) cases were rejected. It is claimed by CBI that accused N. K. Gupta (Accused No.3) along with his wife i.e Accused No.4 Smt. Sangeeta Gupta had entered in to a criminal conspiracy with accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2) and dealing assistant Sh. V. K. Chauhan (deceased) both Dealing Assistants of South Zone, Land & Building Department, GNCT of Delhi in the year 1992 and they created a false application along with false enclosures on 29.12.1992 for allotment of alternative plot in lieu of acquisition of land bearing Khasra no 461/2 of Village Jaitpur, Delhi which was received in the office of L& B Department vide diary no. 7053 dated 29.12.1992. CBI has claimed that investigation has revealed that the said application was written and signed by Accused No. 4 Sangeeta Gupta W/o Sh. N. K. Gupta( Accused No.3) as one Suman. The application was in duplicate and was signed on

In support of her claim as the applicant, accused Sangeeta(Accused No.4) had submitted a false Nakal Jamabandi for the year 1976-77 and 1987-88 signed on 14.01.1991 & 11.10.1992 respectively and false Compensation payment certificate signed &issued on 02.12.1992 by the LAC. The application of Smt. Suman was allotted a number F32(55)/87/92-94/LAB/Alt. It is alleged in the chargesheet that original file of Land and Building Department CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 8 of 210 of this application for allotment was recovered from the residence of accused N. K. Gupta (Accused No. 3) during his house search in Case -RC 2172015AD004/ACU-VI (i.e. RC No 4/ 2015 )a nd was a relied upon document in this case. Thus, the aforesaid original file of Land and Building Department as recovered on house search of Accused No.3 was obtained with permission from the Hon'ble Court for the purpose of investigation of this case.

CBI has claimed that their Investigation has revealed that Sh. Thakar Singh had also applied for the allotment of alternative plot in lieu of his acquired land comprising of land of khasra no. 461/2 on 01.01.1992 with the Land and Building Department and the file number allotted to his application was F. 32(55)41/92-94 in the file head register of the alternative branch of L&B Dept. Investigation by CBI revealed that in the said register, no application was given number F.32(55)87/92-94 in the name of Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev. As per the said register, total 90 applications were received from the farmers of village Jaitpur. Investigation revealed that application number 86 & 87 were missing from the list of applicants in the said register. The said register was being maintained in the Alternative Branch by Dealing Assistant at the time of receipt of application of farmers for allotment of alternative plots during the period of 1992-94 and accused Saroj Bala( Accused No.2) was the dealing assistant at that time in the south zone of Alternative branch. Investigation revealed that the entries in the said register pertaining to village Jaitpur were also made by accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2) and had overwriting in them. CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 9 of 210 Hence, it was claimed that the application bearing number F.32(55)/87/92-94/L&B/Alt was fraudulently created by accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2 ), by abusing her official position as a public servant in connivance with accused Neeru Kumar Gupta (Accused No. 3) and accused Sangeeta Gupta Suman(Accused No.4) to cause unlawful gain to them .

As per the chargesheet, accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2) was working as a Dealing Assistant in South Zone of Land and Building Department and hence, she was the custodian of files of south zone bearing village code 31 to rest of the villages of south zone wherein Village Jaitpur was coded as It was claimed by CBI that it was the accused Saroj Bala who had processed the application and enclosures of applicant Suman D/o Dharam Dev and at the same time, she had also processed the application of Sh. Thakar Singh S/o Sh. Ghuma Singh. During investigation, it was found out that the application and enclosures of Smt. Suman were false and the same were processed by accused Saroj Bala. The verification report viz LAC Report and Tehsildar reports (L&B) were also found to be forged. The LAC Report shown as signed by LAC(ME) on 05.08.1994 and also shown to be issued on 1994 was also found to be forged .The said document was shown as received in Receipt Branch of L&B Dept. on 18.08.1994 vide diary no. 5105. However, during Investigation it was revealed from the Central Diary Register of incoming correspondences that no such report had been received on 1994 CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 10 of 210 as on this date, dairy entry started with diary no. 5659 and no LAC report was received. at diary entry 5105.

It was also revealed that in the file of Sh. Thakar Singh, the LAC report pertaining to his application was signed on 05.08.1994 and issued on 11.08.1994 (at page 117). The said report was received in Receipt branch of L&B Dept. on same day i.e. 11.08.1994 and diary number of 5565 was also found correct as per Central Diary Register. Thus, CBI claimed that the LAC report in the case of Smt. Suman was falsely created after receipt of LAC Report in the case of Sh. Thakar Singh in connivance with the Accused no.2 and same was inserted by her in the file and therefore she actively facilitated the commission of offences as she completed the false documentation by abusing her official position and also placed it before the branch head. It was also claimed that Accused No.2 Saroj Bala being the dealing assistant had first hand knowledge of the crime as she was processing files of both Sh. Thakar Singh and Smt. Suman for the allotment of alternative plot for the same piece of acquired land bearing Khasra no. 461/2 at the same time and thus, her culpability in the crime was crystal clear.

It is the case of CBI that in furtherance to the above said criminal conspiracy, Accused No.1 S. S. Malhi entered into the said conspiracy with Accused No.3 N. K. Gupta and Accused No.4 Sangeeta Gupta; who impersonated as Suman, d/o Dharamdev for fraudulent allotment of alternative plot in her name. Accused No.1 started working in Alternative Branch from June 1997. It was found out that the application of Suman was pending since 19.06.1995 and CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 11 of 210 on 18.06.1997, accused No.1 fraudulently and in conspiracy with other accused initiated the note dated 18.6.1997 with a dishonest intention to get an Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 alternative plot allotted in the name of Suman despite the fact that she was neither the owner of the acquired land nor had received any compensation in lieu of its acquisition. As per charge-sheet, it was revealed that land bearing Khasra no. 461/2 was owned by Sh. Thakar Singh and Sh. Laabh Singh and Thakar Singh had received the compensation for entire Khasra no. 461/2, Village Jaitpur at the time of its acquisition. It was revealed that even the process for allotment of alternative plot in lieu of acquired land of K No. 461/2 , Village Jaitpur in the name of Sh.Thakar Singh was also dealt by Accused No.1 during the same period and in furtherance to the above said criminal conspiracy, on 18.06.1997 Accused No.1 submitted a note before the branch head asking for approval that both files of Suman and one Bhanu as part owners of Khasra No 461/2 , Village Jaitpur may be allowed to be proceeded with further and the applicants may be requested to submit an affidavit with regard to personal hearing and as a consequence thereof , Smt.

Shashi Kaushal, the then Dy. Secretary (Alt.) approved the same and a letter dated 18.06.1997 was sent to Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev in this regard. It was found out that in furtherance of the said criminal conspiracy, after a gap of one year I.e. on 13.07.1998, after joining of Sh. H. R. Sapra as Dy. Secretary (Alt), Accused No.1 proposed that the applicant be asked upon to submit her affidavit regarding her personal hearing in the department and thus, a fair letter was placed by him before Sh. H. R. Sapra. The letter was approved on 15.07.1998 by Sh. H. R. Sapra and on 23.11.1998, CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 12 of 210 Accused No.1 put up a note to Sh. H. R. Sapra that requisite documents have been received and the cases are complete so a fresh Check memo may be allowed to be prepared. The same was approved by branch head on 23.11.1998. Thereafter, accused No.1 prepared a Check memo and obtained clearance from all zones by declaring that no older complete files were left out and no other claim in respect of same piece of land was pending in other zones. As per the chargesheet, in the said check memo prepared by Accused No.1,he falsely mentioned about the payment of compensation to Suman on 09.11.1992. and also showed Suman as the recorded owner of land bearing Khasra no 461/2 at the time of notification u/s 4 of LA Act. It is claimed by CBI that all these false details were mentioned in Check memo prepared and signed by Accused no.1 dated 26.11.1998 and thereafter, on 27.11.1998 , he submitted a detailed note before Sh. H. R. Sapra wherein he proposed to obtain opinion of ALA which was marked to ALA by Sh. H. R. Sapra on 30.10.1998.

It was also revealed that in the file of Sh. Thakar Singh, the LAC report pertaining to his application was signed on 05.08.1994 and issued on 11.08.1994 (at page 117). The said report was received in Receipt branch of L&B Dept. on same day i.e. 11.08.1994 and diary number of 5565 was also found correct as per Central Diary Register. Thus, CBI claimed that the LAC report in the case of Smt. Suman was falsely created after receipt of LAC Report in the case of Sh. Thakar Singh in connivance with the Accused no.2 and same was inserted by her in the file and therefore she actively facilitated the commission of offences as she completed the false documentation by abusing her official position and also placed it before the branch head. It was also claimed that Accused No.2 Saroj Bala being the dealing assistant had first hand knowledge of the crime as she was processing files of both Sh. Thakar Singh and Smt. Suman for the allotment of alternative plot for the same piece of acquired land bearing Khasra no. 461/2 at the same time and thus, her culpability in the crime was crystal clear.

It is the case of CBI that Sh. Diwakar Singh, ALA had recommended for consideration of the case before the recommendation committee as per the noting made in the file by accused No.1 and he also suggested a time frame for obtaining response of the applicant as there was gap of more than one year. On receipt of this ALA opinon, Sh. H. R. Sapra noted on 02.12.1998 that case file of co-owner Bhanu linked with this file had not been seen by the ALA and Assistant may be asked to take back the file to the ALA for his comments on the linked file. CBI has claimed that Accused No.1 in furtherance to the CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 13 of 210 said criminal conspiracy made a false declaration on the note sheet that file of the co-owner Bhanu had been seen by ALA who had desired to put up the linked file of Smt. Bhanu before the recommendation committee. He also suggested that both the files of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu to be placed before the recommendation committee, which noting was approved by Sh. H. R. Sapra on 17.12.1998. In furtherance to the said criminal Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 conspiracy, Accused No.1 prepared a check list and summary sheet, duly signed/initialed by him for being placed before the recommendation committee for allotment of alternative plot in the name of Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev. It is alleged that Accused No.1 knowingly and deliberately prepared the noting and check memo in which false details were mentioned by him and on the basis of the said documents containing false information, the recommendation committee recommended the allotment of the plot in the name of Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev.

Thus, CBI has claimed that in furtherance to the said criminal conspiracy, by working dishonestly, knowingly and deliberately, Accused No.1 prepared the recommendation letter No. 001113 dated 19.02.1999 and initialed on the same and placed it before Sh. H. R. Sapra and got it signed from Smt. Asha Nayar, Joint Secretary (L&B). Thereafter, the said letter was sent to the Commissioner, Delhi Development Authority, Vikas Sadan, INA New Delhi wherein it was requested to allot a plot measuring 80 sq. yds to Smt. Suman and by issuing this letter, Smt. Suman had become entitled for allotment of alternative plot from DDA in her name. CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 14 of 210 It is the case of CBI that Accused No.1 Sh. Swarn Singh Malhi was the custodian of the files of South Zone, Alternative Branch, Land and Building Dept. during his tenure in said zone. Investigation has also revealed that after issuance of recommendation letter in the name of Smt. Suman to DDA, the file should have been consigned to Central Record Room of Land &Building Department but the same was not done by Accused No.1 and instead the file was found in possession of accused N. K. Gupta and his wife accused Sangeeta Gupta when the same was recovered during their house search in RC No. 2172015A0004/ACU-Vi/ RC No 4/2015. CBI has claimed that accused N. K. Gupta was the mastermind of this crime and he used to frequently visit the Alternative Branch of Land and building Department to meet with accused No.1. CBI has claimed that their investigation has revealed that the said applicant Smt. Suman was none other than the wife of Accused No.3, i.e accused No.4 Sangeeta Gupta.

During investigation, the enclosures of the application of Smt. Suman which were submitted to Land & Building Dept. were sent to CFSL with specimens of accused N. K. Gupta and accused Sangeeta Gupta . The expert had opined that the writing in hindi on the Nakal Jamabandi were that of accused N. K. Gupta. Hence ,CBI claimed that Accused No.3 had actively participated in commission of the alleged offence. The accused Sangeeta Gupta W/o accused N. K Gupta was found to be the applicant who impersonated herself as Suman D/o Dharam Dev R/o Chirag Delhi. Neither Accused No.3 or Accused No.4 nor Suman were found to be the owners of land bearing CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 15 of 210 Khasra no. 461/2 , Village Jaitpur nor any land of Suman or Sangeeta Gupta had ever been acquired or any compensation was paid to her in lieu of the same. However, Accused No.4 dishonestly and knowingly submitted an application in the name of Smt. Suman dated 16.12.1992 which was shown as received in Department on the same date and all Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 the enclosures of the said application were false and were containing false details. During investigation, CFSL expert had given positive incriminating opinion on the signature / handwritings of accused Sangeeta Gupta appearing as that of "Suman" on the exhibits. It was also found out that Accused No.4 had also provided her coloured photographs which were found attached with the said recommendation letter No. 001113 dated 19.02.1999 sent to DDA for allotment of alternative plot in the name of "Suman" by Land and Building Department after culmination of the meeting dated 15.1

CBI has claimed that Accused No.4 impersonated herself as Smt. Suman and provided false residential address and when DDA sent Demand Cum Allotment Letter bearing no. F. 27 [11/1999/LSB(R)/9479 dated 09.08.02 to this address, it was returned with remarks as " incomplete address". When DDA attempted to deliver the said letter through a person, the address was found to be non-existent and thus, it was found out that Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev R/o Chirag Delhi was "non- existant". Sh. H. R. Sapra, the then Deputy Director of Land and Building Department was named as an accused in the FIR. CBI has claimed that investigation revealed that he had worked as Dy. CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 16 of 210 Secretary (Alt) in Alternative Branch of L&B Department for the period 1997 to June, 1999 and when he joined the Alternative Branch, Accused No.1 was the dealing assistant of the south zone of the branch and he was the one dealing with the file of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu which was already in process in the section. It was revealed that the verification had already been completed by accused Saroj Bala and accused S S Malhi. It was on

1997 that the last note-sheet entry asking for approval that both files may be allowed to be proceeded with further and the applicants may be requested to submit affidavit in current date regarding their personal hearing was filed, which was approved by Smt. Shashi Kaushal, Dy Secretary (Alt). On joining of Sh. H R. Sapra, Accused No.1 again put up a fair letter asking applicants to submit requisite documents/information. The noting of Accused No. 1 was routed through Sh. Brinda Ban Gupta, Office Supt. on 17.07.1998 and Sh. H. R. Sapra approved the same on that very date. Thereafter, accused no.1 submitted to Sh. H. R. Sapra that requisite documents had been received and now cases were complete and a fresh check memo be allowed to be prepared. This noting was approved by Sh. H. R. Sapra on 23.11.1998 and thereafter, Accused No.1 prepared a check memo under his signature dated 26.11.1998 and thereafter it was certified on 14.01.1999, one day prior to scheduled meeting of recommendation committee that no older complete file was left out. It was after preparation of check memo dated 26.11.1998 that Accused No.1 also prepared detailed note in the note sheet on 27.11.1998 and put it up before Sh. H. R. Sapra for obtaining ALA report. Accordingly. Sh. H. R. Sapra marked the file to ALA on CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 17 of 210 30.11.1998 for examination from legal angle. On receipt of file from ALA, Sh. H. R. Sapra noted on 02.12.1998 that the case file of the co - owner linked with this file had not been seen by the ALA. He marked the file to Dealing Assistant (AD) that DA may please take back the file to the ALA for his comments on the linked file. On this, on

1990, Accused No.1 made a false declaration on the note sheet that file of co-owner had been seen by ALA claiming that he desired to put up the linked file of Smt. Bhanu before the Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 recommendation committee. It is alleged that thereafter, Accused No.1 suggested that both the files of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu be placed before the recommendation committee and Sh. H. R. Sapra approved the same on 17.12.1998. Thereafter, the both cases of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu were recommended in the meeting of recommendation committee held 15.01.1999.CBI has claimed that their investigation has revealed that Sh. H R Sapra acted in good faith on the noting of Accused No.1 and during investigation, the evidence of criminal conspiracy of Sh. H. R. Sapra could not be found. During searches also, no link evidence was found against Sh. H. R. Sapra and thus, he was placed in column no. 12 of the charge-sheet and was instead cited as a prosecution witness of this case. It is a matter of record that he expired during trial of this case.

K. Gupta (Accused No.3) to use the forged document as genuine, dishonestly, knowingly and fraudulently to cause unlawful gain to them. Accused no. 1 S. S. Malhi had stated the following in his statement recorded u/s. 313 Cr.P.C. as his defence :- "They have wrongly deposed. The same is explained herein below. The below mentioned explanation may be considered as my Statement under Section 313 (5) of the Cr.P.C, 1973. CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 65 of 210 a. Most of the witnesses who were my seniors such as the members of the committee and other senior officials have deposed as if the decision making of the entire department was on me. I am a graduate only and I was posted as an Upper Division Clerk (UDC) holding the office of Dealing Assistant in the Alternative Branch of the Land & Building Department. There were multiple persons who were higher than me in hierarchy such as the Office Superintendent (PW- 34) followed by Deputy Secretary [who is a DANICS Officer] followed by Additional Secretary [IAS Officer], followed by Secretary - cum Commissioner [Head of the Department, a Senior IAS Official] whereas the Committee which was to decide and Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 recommend the cases comprised of - (i) Secretary (Land), (ii) Additional Secretary (L&B), (iii) Deputy Secretary (Alt) and (iv) Assistant Legal Advisor (L&B) [who is an advocate]. b. Additionally, the Recommendation Committee acted as an independent body making recommendations which was also preceded by reports made from three different sub-divisions which were the LAC, Tehsildar and the Writ/Legal Cell. These reports were prepared by specialist departments/offices that is the LAC office, Naib Tehsildar and the Legal Department of the Land and Building Department.

I did not have any role in preparation of these reports as they were prepared by the respective specialized departments. The job of the Dealing Assistant was at best of indexing the said reports and placing the same before the high authorities. Since these reports were prepared by persons holding higher posts and qualifications than me, I was in no position to take accept or reject or scrutinize these reports on the contents and its merit. These reports could therefore have only been accepted or rejected or scrutinized by senior/higher officials who had decision making power. I also state that I was not tasked with physical verification of the applicants. c. It is the case of various Prosecution Witnesses that they merely relied upon the summary sheet made by me and my predecessors, which was made available at the time of the meeting. However, a careful look at the summary sheet would show that the same is merely in the form of an index or as the name suggest as a "summary". The contents of these CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 66 of 210 reports were never reproduced in the said summary sheet and it was merely the page number of the report was indicated. Merely the reference of a page number in the summary sheet shows that the same was only an index which guided the reader to the particular page of the file where the report was placed. By no means can the indication of the page number can be construed as any opinion on the opinion on the said report. Therefore, the witnesses of the Recommendation Committee, who are the actual decision makers, have falsely deposed against me for reasons best known to them.

It appears that they have taken advantage of the fact that there was no written memorandum or procedure which governed the process of recommendation and have simply blamed me, being the Dealing Assistant. If the statements of these witnesses are taken to be true, it will lead to a fallacious situation that the report/documents made by high ranking and specialized officials [DANICS Officers, Advocates and Tehsildars] will be let to the mercy of an UDC who otherwise no decision-making powers or specialization has to comment upon these reports. Additionally, the statements to the effect that the committee during its deliberations only went through the summary sheet and not the files is also illogical and doubtful because the summary sheet itself made references to particular page numbers within the file. If the file was not present during the meeting, the summary sheet itself would be rendered redundant as the reference to the page numbers would be of no consequence. d. There is also an allegation that various entries in the check list/summary sheet were falsely made by me. This is incorrect as the file in the present case, predated my posting in the branch and had been initiated by my predecessors. During the Cross Examination of the Investigation Officer (PW-47) on my behalf, it has come to light that the summary sheet in fact is based on the already existing check list/summary sheet and the same references have been made to the specific pages of Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 the already existing file. It is not the case of the Prosecution that a new file with new documents was prepared by me. Therefore, I cannot be held liable for making false entries in the check list/summary sheet." CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.

During the course of final arguments, Ld. Defence counsel contended that after incorporation of Sec. 311 A Cr .P.C in the year 2006 , only a magistrate could order a person including the accused to give his specimen signatures and handwritings for the purpose of investigation whereas in the present case ,no such order was obtained by the IO from the concerned magistrate/ Special Judge and hence, the processes vide which the specimen samples were obtained from the Accused No. 3 and Accused No.4 in this case were not in consonance with due course of law .However , the court is not in agreement with the interpretation meted out by the defence with regard to legality of actions Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 of the CBI in this regard. Sec 311 A CrPC is an enabling provision which comes to the aid of the investigating agency when a suspect or an accused refuses to give his specimen handwriting CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 151 of 210 / signatures during investigation. The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed in the case of Kathi Kalu Oghad (AIR 1961 SC 1808) that giving of specimen signatures and handwriting to the police will not amount to testimonial compulsion as prohibited by Article 20(3) of the Indian Constitution. The Supreme Court judgment provided a nuanced interpretation of Article 20(3), balancing individual constitutional protection against self-incrimination with the needs of effective criminal investigation. By distinguishing between testimonial and material evidence, the Court affirmed that provision of fingerprints, specimen writings, or signatures does not constitute self-incrimination, provided there is no coercion involved.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has also observed time and again that merely giving a specimen handwriting does not amount to giving a statement so as to be hit by Sec 162 CrPC. In the case of Vinay Tyagi Vs Irshad Ali ( 2013)5SC 762 ,the Supreme Court observed that when a police officer obtains the specimens signatures /handwritings from a witness or suspect or accused, he does not violate any statutory provisions or provisions of Constitution of India .The investigating officer is thus entitled to take specimen signatures and handwriting of the accused provided the accused is willing to furnish the same in compliance of request of the police officer to do so. The act of a police officer in taking specimen signature and handwriting is an act of collection of evidence and in case the accused voluntarily consents to giving his specimens for the aid of investigation, it will not be barred by any statute or be in derogation of Indian Constitution. The Supreme Court in the case of Murari Lal v. State of M.P. (1979 INSC 248, decided on November 21, 1979) established several crucial principles regarding the evidentiary value of handwriting expert testimony wherein they rejected the notion that handwriting expert evidence should be treated with inherent suspicion or requires mandatory corroboration in all cases. The judgment clarified that a handwriting expert is "no accomplice" and their testimony should not be automatically condemned to a lower class of evidence. While doing so the Court acknowledged that handwriting analysis is an imperfect science compared to more developed forensic CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 159 of 210 techniques like fingerprint analysis therefore there was a higher risk of an incorrect opinion. Hence, the courts were cautioned to probe the reasons for the opinion and consider all other relevant evidence and decide finally to accept or reject it. Nevertheless, the judgment emphasized that in cases where the expert's reasoning was convincing and there was no reliable contradictory evidence, uncorroborated testimony may be accepted. The Court emphasized that an expert's opinion should be tested by the acceptability of the reasons given by him rather than being viewed with initial suspicion. The Apex court held that - "Expert testimony is made relevant by Section 45 of the Evidence Act and where the Court has to form an opinion upon a point as to identity of handwriting, the opinion of a person "specially skilled" "in questions as to identity of handwriting" is expressly made a relevant fact...So, corroboration may not invariably be insisted upon before acting on the opinion of an handwriting expert and there need be no initial suspicion. But, on the facts of a particular case, a court may require corroboration of a varying degree".

In the present case, Ld. Defence counsel for Accused No. 3 and Accused No.4 placed reliance upon a case titled as Sunil Chaudhary Vs. Arup Kumar Ghosh ( AIR 2006 CALCUTTA 109) wherein the court observed that the opinion of a handwriting expert was generally of frail character and hence too much weightage should not be given to it. However , in the very same order, the court had also observed that there was no hard and fast rule of prudence which had been crystalized into a rule of law that opinion of a handwriting expert CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 160 of 210 must never be acted upon unless corroborated. It was observed in this referred case that the reasons given by the expert must be carefully probed and examined and all relevant evidence must be considered . It was also made clear that in cases where the reasons of the opinion were convincing and no reliable evidence was throwing doubt, the uncorroborated testimony of the expert could be accepted. Recently , in an appeal decided by the Apex Court titled as C. Kamalakkannan v. State Of Tamil Nadu ( 2025 INSC 309) , the expert opinion used by the lower courts to return a finding of guilt upon the accused was set aside by observing that as the prosecution failed to lead primary evidence in form of the original postal cover, trial Court could not have concluded that the prosecution had succeeded in proving that the handwriting on the disputed document was that of the accused appellant. In this case, the Supreme Court had to examine whether the prosecution had proven that the postal cover in question bore the Appellant's handwriting.

The reliance of prosecution upon the testimony of a handwriting expert without producing the original postal cover in evidence was the basis of reversing the findings of conviction .As has been observed in the case of Murari Lal that each case has to be dealt with on the basis of its peculiar facts , similarly in the case of Kamalkannana, the apex court frowned upon the reliance of the prosecution on the sole testimony of the handwriting expert in the absence of the original / primary piece of evidence .The rationale behind requirement of independent corroboration to the testimony of a handwriting expert lies in the fact that handwriting expert opinion like all sciences is based upon human judgment, which is fallible as there might be an occasion when an CBI Vs. In the case of Fakhruddin Vs State of Madhya Pradesh ( AIR 1967 Supreme Court 1326) Hon'ble Supreme Court held Both under Sections 45 and 47 Indian Evidence Act , the report of an expert is an opinion, in the former by a scientific comparison and in the latter on the basis of familiarity resulting from frequent observations and experience and in either case, the Court must satisfy itself by such means as are open that the opinion may be acted upon.

In order to decide whether sanction is necessary, the test employed is to see whether the act complained off is totally unconnected or whether there is a reasonable connection with the official duty of the public servant. If each and every act committed by the accused is construed in discharge of his official duty, the legislative intent of enactment of this Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 provision would be frustrated. P.C being accorded to public servants lies in the fact that State functions through its officers and each officer should be able to achieve public good by exercise of power vested upon them. The intent behind providing protection to the public servant is to enable him to exercise the power of the sovereign fearlessly provided the actions are bona fide. Needless to state that the exercise of this power is subject to discretion but the exercise of power can never be arbitrary to the extent of being criminal.

The Hon'ble Delhi High Court had observed in the case of Runu Ghosh Vs. CBI (Crl. Appeal No. 482/2002 , decided on 21.12.2011) with respect to provisions of Sec. 13(1) (d) (iii) of PC Act that what was vital to the prosecution to prove its case was to establish that the actions of the public servant and decisions which resulted in a third party obtaining a pecuniary advantage or valuable thing were done without public interest. When a public servant's decision exhibits manifest disregard to the interest of the public resulting in pecuniary advantage or vesting of a valuable thing with a third party, liability for criminal misconduct arises qua the said public servant u/s. 13 (1) (d) (iii) of PC Act. This provision does not require proof of intent as the only act made punishable by the Parliament is act done against public interest. Thus, the applicability of Sec. 13 (2) of PC Act which CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 202 of 210 punishes the act of criminal misconduct by a public servant does not depend on the fact of the public servant having obtained a pecuniary advance or valuable thing for himself. The ingredients of the Section 13(1)(d) are attracted if the public servant by his action causes a third party to obtain an advantage by harming the public interest. Public servants are obliged to act in a manner which is fair, just and equitable as they hold the property of the State in their hands for general welfare of the public by acting as trustees of the same. The level of trust reposed in public servants by the society must be reflected in their high standards of behavior and the same is expected out of them in discharge of their official duties as well. Hence, an action of a public servant exhibiting disregard to the public interest with corresponding result of unlawful gain to a third party is to be necessarily construed as an act of criminal misconduct by the said public servant.

Sec. 419 of IPC provides for punishment for whoever cheats by personation whereas Sec. 420 of IPC provides for punishment to whoever cheats and by such cheating dishonestly induces the person so cheated to deliver any property to any person or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of the valuable security or anything which is signed or sealed and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security. Sec. 415 of IPC defines cheating as whoever by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that person shall retain any property or intentionally induces a person so deceived to do or to omit from doing anything which he would not do or omit to do if CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors. CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 204 of 210 he were not so deceived and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage to that person in body, mind, reputation or property is set to cheat that person. The explanation of this section provides that a dishonest concealment of facts is a deception within the meaning of this section.

It is germane to observe that the definition of offence of cheating also embraces certain situations in which no transfer of property has been occasioned by the said deception. In the case of Iridium India Telecom Ltd. Vs. Motorola Incorporated (AIR 2011 SCC 20), it was held that misleading statements which have the effect of withholding vital facts as a result of which a person has been intentionally induced to do or to omit from doing something will amount to deception. It was also held in this case that non-disclosure of relevant information will be treated as mis-representation of facts which would also amount to deception. In other words, if somebody by his actions causes the other person to believe something which is false or misleading Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025 and is erroneous, it will amount to deception. Suffice to say that Mens rea on the part of the person deceiving has to be established by clear evidence in all cases.
